The first 12-hourly run (08:22–08:28 UTC, 7 November) did not advance any outstanding issue. The scheduled Codex agent ran collection, delivered one alert and then stopped. Its report said "I did not advance the outstanding issues in this run". Prose instructions alone (PRs #29 and #33) are not enough. This PR turns the advance step into a loop the agent repeats, and makes completion depend on it.

- **`advance-next`:** a new `stack_monitor.py advance-next --file {holder, pass_started_at}` command. Each call selects and claims the next active issue, then writes its private dossier. It returns `remaining` until it reports `done: true`.
  - Issues are taken in this order: awaiting verification, investigating, awaiting approval, then blocked.
  - It skips issues claimed by another holder, and issues already advanced since `pass_started_at`.
  - It rejects a pass start in the future or more than 24 hours old.
- **`finish`:** reports `unadvanced_count`, and returns `next_required_step: advance_issue` while any active issue has not been handled since the current collection. `complete` now requires that every issue was advanced, matching the owner's requirement.
- **Prose:** the scheduled workflow's advance step is now a short loop with explicit stop conditions and optional parallel workers. Each worker has its own holder, and claims prevent overlap. The completion table gains an `advance_issue` row.
- **Unchanged:** the approval and containment guards; the advance step still authorizes no device change.

work_request.title: feat(checks)!: audit every lock file, whole repository, every run
work_request.request:
The dependency audit now covers every lock file in the repository on every commit and every CI run.

- **Discovered scope.** `check-toolchain-parity.py audit` enumerates manifests and lock files from `git_inventory` and excludes only `is_fixture_program` paths. It recognises uv, poetry, Pipfile, `requirements*.txt`, npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, Cargo, Go, Bundler and Composer files.
- **Fail closed.**
  - `uv.lock`: `uv export --project <dir> --locked --all-extras --all-groups --all-packages`, then the pinned pip-audit (`--strict --disable-pip --no-deps`).
  - `requirements*.txt`: the same pip-audit route.
  - `package-lock.json` / `npm-shrinkwrap.json`: `npm audit --json --package-lock-only --include=dev --include=optional --include=peer --prefix <dir>`.
  - Any other recognised lock format: `no auditor for <path>`.
  - A manifest that declares dependencies with no lock of its ecosystem beside it, and that no lock covers (uv path sources, npm workspaces): `unpinned dependencies in <path>`.
  - A lock with only local packages skips the auditor. An empty export of a lock that has third-party packages is a finding.
- **Whole repo, every run.** The staged-file trigger, `--ci` and `AUDIT_ARGS` are gone. `gate-ci` runs `gate-commit` unchanged.
- **Every advisory blocks.** Every audit line starts with the rule ID and follows the harness catalogue contract (oh-mi-pi-config PR #152). The format is documented in the checker docstring and defined as `ADVISORY_LINE` and `FAILURE_LINE`:

  ```
  SECURITY.dependency-audit lock=<lock-path> ecosystem=<osv-ecosystem> package=<name> version=<exact-locked-version> advisory=<advisory-id> aliases=<id>,<id> fix=<version>,<version>
  SECURITY.dependency-audit failure=<kind> path=<repo-path> reason=<text-to-end-of-line>
  ```

  - `ecosystem` uses OSV names (`PyPI`, `npm`).
  - `failure` is one of `unknown-lock-format`, `manifest-without-lock`, `exception` or `auditor`. The pip-audit pin findings and the audit-mode crash path also use the `auditor` form.
  - For npm, `fix` is the lowest published release above the locked version that falls outside the GHSA vulnerable range (`npm view <pkg> versions`). This runs only for vulnerable packages.
  - **Malicious packages.** Suppose npm audit marks an advisory malicious (CWE-506, or a title that starts with "Malicious"), and no `MAL-` record exists for it. The finding then gains the alias `MAL-<advisory-id>`. Existing `MAL-` IDs or aliases are not duplicated.
- **Exceptions.** `scripts/checks/dependency-audit-exceptions.json` starts empty (`{"schemaVersion": 1, "exceptions": []}`). An entry suppresses one advisory only when all of these hold:
  - It has exactly the fields `advisory`, `package`, `version`, `lock`, `reason`, `exposure` and `expires`.
  - It has not expired.
  - The package version still matches the lock.
  - It matches a current finding, by advisory ID or alias.
  - That advisory has no fix.
  Otherwise the entry is a finding and suppresses nothing.

evidence.tested:
`orchestrator/tests/test_dependency_audit.py` (fast tier) builds a repository layout in tmp with these parts:
- nested uv and npm locks, including a uv path member and an npm workspace
- a Cargo lock with no auditor
- manifests without a lock
- a fixture-program lock that the audit must ignore

It asserts exact findings and auditor commands. It also covers the advisory-line format and its parsing, npm fix computation, fail-closed report and exit handling, and every exception rule. Auditor subprocesses are stubbed. The old `--ci` and staged-path tests are removed.

work_request.title: feat(security-stack-monitor): add advance-next loop and require advancement before completion
work_request.request:
The first 12-hourly run (08:22–08:28 UTC, 7 November) did not advance any outstanding issue. The scheduled Codex agent ran collection, delivered one alert and then stopped. Its report said "I did not advance the outstanding issues in this run". Prose instructions alone (PRs #29 and #33) are not enough. This PR turns the advance step into a loop the agent repeats, and makes completion depend on it.

- **`advance-next`:** a new `stack_monitor.py advance-next --file {holder, pass_started_at}` command. Each call selects and claims the next active issue, then writes its private dossier. It returns `remaining` until it reports `done: true`.
  - Issues are taken in this order: awaiting verification, investigating, awaiting approval, then blocked.
  - It skips issues claimed by another holder, and issues already advanced since `pass_started_at`.
  - It rejects a pass start in the future or more than 24 hours old.
- **`finish`:** reports `unadvanced_count`, and returns `next_required_step: advance_issue` while any active issue has not been handled since the current collection. `complete` now requires that every issue was advanced, matching the owner's requirement.
- **Prose:** the scheduled workflow's advance step is now a short loop with explicit stop conditions and optional parallel workers. Each worker has its own holder, and claims prevent overlap. The completion table gains an `advance_issue` row.
- **Unchanged:** the approval and containment guards; the advance step still authorizes no device change.

evidence.tested:
- **Repo gate:** `scripts/gate.sh` passed (markdownlint, Python suites, path check).
- **Replay of a real run:** the test run's artifacts (8 URLs logged across 3 questions, two analysis passes) went through normalize, validate, reconcile, citations, constraints and report with the fixed scripts.
  - Consensus went from 6 single-pass findings (`needs-followup`) to 3 findings agreed by both passes (`pass`).
  - An injected same-question duplicate was removed; report says "Distinct sources logged: 8" with 8 references (was 16).
  - A finding on a different claim stayed separate and marked absent from the other pass.
  - The report refused a `fail` validation report and a citation report made before `analysis.json` changed.

work_request.title: feat(security-stack-monitor): record owner requests and add owner-report
work_request.request:
The owner had no reliable way to see which security issues are waiting on him. The register's `owner` field is free text such as "security-audit and device owner", so a list of issues needing the owner could only be guessed from wording. This PR adds a structured owner request and a report that lists those requests.

- **Owner request:** `issue-update` accepts an optional `owner_request: {kind: approval|decision|information, request}`. It is validated and stored in the meta table as `owner_request:<id>`, so the schema does not change. Each `issue-update` replaces or clears it, so a request never outlives the handling that raised it.
  - `awaiting_approval` now requires a request of kind `approval`.
  - Issues in terminal states (resolved, accepted risk, excluded by policy) reject a request.
- **Report:** the new read-only mode `stack_monitor.py owner-report` lists active issues that have a request, approvals first, with counts by kind.
- **Docs:**
  - Remediation explains when to set a request.
  - The hourly report includes the owner-report counts.
  - `SKILL.md` gains a "Review what needs the owner" entry.
- **Unchanged:** the issue schema, the allowed state changes, and all evidence rules.
